additional_concerns: All six extracted claims are supported by the supplied source, subject to their stated role and activity conditions; paragraph 17's SHOULD classification represents the directive reminder rather than a literal modal verb.

The three request-based candidates make a paragraph 14 demonstration request necessary and sufficient for a TRUE_IS_SATISFIED result, without source support for treating a request as performance or for using that request to trigger the distinct paragraph 15 and 16 duties.
The three constant-true candidates declare satisfaction for every in-scope provider without assessing conduct or outcomes; the source does not authorize that unconditional conclusion.

Paragraph 14 distinguishes confirmation from demonstration upon request, while footnote 5 jointly describes confirmation and demonstration; their possible attachment readings do not justify either unconditional satisfaction or satisfaction from the request alone.

No SFC demonstration request does not establish failure or fulfilment of ongoing responsibilities, confirmation, register maintenance, or applicable intermediary duties, and does not establish whether a separate audit or legal-opinion request exists.

Paragraph 10, footnote 1 and the ownership-record provision distinguish retained provider responsibility from delegated register maintenance and actual operational and record-keeping outcomes; none of the candidates assesses these distinctions.

The additional address-notification requirement in section 6.8 is distinct from register maintenance, and section 6.11C's selection, monitoring and supervision duties concern third-party valuation within their own scope; neither supplies a general satisfaction standard for these candidates.

Footnote 5 references paragraphs 10 to 13, but their full contents and the referenced Appendix factors are not supplied, so complete substantive compliance cannot be established from this packet or from the candidates' externally supplied scope classifications.
